messages:
ana_support: :rotating_light: FYI — several EU customers reporting large latency jumps (P95 ~300-800ms) and intermittent 401s since ~08:10 UTC. Customers say requests appear to hit US IPs. Anyone else seeing cross-region answers?

matt_sre: saw an uptick in cross-region routing around 08:12. Edge metrics show a spike of answers from us-west for eu queries. Filing quick traces now.

ana_support: customer_ops forwarded a trace from a Dutch ISP: 'trace shows hops to 34.78.12.45 (us-west) instead of expected eu address' — customer reports auth failures and billing spike.

customer_ops: pasted customer snippet: "curl -v https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' --connect-timeout 2" -> long connect + 401. They ran `dig` and got: 
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.ai +short
34.78.12.45
```
Expected eu IP was `18.136.45.21`.

deploy-bot: [alert] geoip-routing-anomaly detected (rule: answer-pop-mismatch) - incident INC-1234 created: https://console.redwood.ai/edge/geoip/incident/INC-1234

jules_net: quick theory: some EU resolvers are returning answers without EDNS client-subnet, or ISP-level NAT is collapsing ECS, so our GeoIP fallback is picking a safe default which is resolving to us-west gateway IPs. Also seeing different GeoIP DB versions on a couple of edge nodes (v2023.11 vs v2024.03) — could be a stale sync.

prakash_eng: can you paste a raw `dig +short +norecurse @<resolver>` from one of affected clients? Also want the full `dig +norecurse +noedns` and `dig +short +edns=0` outputs if available.

customer_ops: here's a captured repro from the ISP (NetNL):
```
$ dig @195.80.200.1 inference.redwood.ai +norecurse
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
inference.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 34.78.12.45
;; AUTHORITY SECTION: 
;; ADDITIONAL SECTION:
```
No ECS in additional. TTL=300.

dave_customer: noted that when they used a VPN to EU host the IP resolved to `18.136.45.21` and latency returned to normal. So seems resolver-side.

matt_sre: I pulled edge node logs for eu-west-1; some nodes still referencing geoip DB `v2023.11` while newer nodes have `v2024.03`. That could make a small subset of our anycast population answer with older location mapping.

jules_net: also found evidence of ISP-level DNS cache with long TTLs — many ISPs ignore our 300 TTL and hold answers longer. If the old answer was a US IP, they'll keep handing it out.

prakash_eng: short-term mitigations:
- Force update GeoIP DB on all edge nodes (rollout job queued).
- Add a temporary routing policy: if incoming request's TLS SNI or client IP subnet maps to EU but answer is non-EU, prefer the eu gateway (prefer-region policy) for 1 hour.
- Ask customer to set `X-Region: eu` header as a workaround (we can honor header for authenticated tenants).

ana_support: I've already told customers to try the header workaround; they confirmed it reduces latency. I'll send an official note.

jules_net: action items:
- I'll open a ticket with GeoIP provider re: v2024.03 vs v2023.11 sync mismatch (assigned to jules_net).
- matt_sre, can you push the emergency prefer-region rule to all control-plane nodes?

matt_sre: yes, prepping a constrained rollout with canary -> full. Will monitor auth errors after toggle.

prakash_eng: also suggest we audit our fallback rules: currently if ECS absent we choose a safe-pop default which appears to be us-west for some prefixes. We should adjust safe-pop mapping to use continent-level preference when ECS missing. I'll open PR.

customer_ops: noted some customers also saw billing spikes due to repeated retries while requests hit wrong region and got 401s. Finance wants an estimate of affected token counts.

ana_support: collected per-customer logs and forwarded to finance. Estimated ~12k token-equivalent across 3 customers during the 20-minute window.

matt_sre: rolled prefer-region canary to 10% at 08:35 UTC — canaries show drop in cross-region answers for affected resolvers. No increase in 5xx. Will expand to 100% in 15 mins if stable.

deploy-bot: [deploy] prefer-region routing config v1.2 -> canary (10%) by matt_sre at 08:35 UTC

jules_net: GeoIP DB full refresh job completed at 08:42 UTC — all nodes now show v2024.03. That seemed to cut the remaining mismatches.

prakash_eng: PR opened to change default-safe-pop mapping: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821 (will run in next deploy).

ana_support: customer update sent: "We're investigating a GeoIP routing discrepancy that caused some EU traffic to route to US gateways. Workarounds: set `X-Region: eu` header or use EU host. We're deploying fixes — expect resolution within 30 minutes." They replied :thumbsup:.

customer_ops: customer follow-up: latency back to normal after ~08:45 UTC, auth failures stopped. They want root-cause note.

matt_sre: root-cause (preliminary): combination of stale GeoIP DB on a fraction of edge nodes + ISP resolvers ignoring TTLs + ECS being stripped by some ISPs -> some client resolvers continued serving an old US IP for our host. Mitigations implemented: GeoIP refresh, prefer-region routing, adjust fallback mapping, and longer-term: improve ECS-aware fallback and telemetry to detect stale answer hotspots.

jules_net: logging ticket created to add resolver-level telemetry (which resolver IP returned the answer) to help correlate in future.

ana_support: closing loop with customers now. Will add post-incident note to #postmortems.

prakash_eng: leaving this open for 24h monitoring. If anyone sees a re-occurrence, ping me.

matt_sre: marking incident INC-1234 as mitigated at 08:50 UTC.

ana_support: thanks all — great fast work. :heart:
